title: To Thee, My God and Saviour
description: To Thee, My God and Saviour in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 646 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thee, my God and Sa-viour, My soul ex-ult-ing sings; Re-joic-ing in thy fa-vor, Al-might-y King of kings! I'll cel-e-brate thy glo-ry With all thy saints a-bove. And tell the joy-ful sto-ry Of thy re-deem-ing love.

lines: To Thee, my God and Saviour,
Soon as the morn with roses
And to my soul draw near.
My soul shall feel thy blessing

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
